steps: Shape your dominant hand into an A, with the thumb sticking up alongside the fist.
Bring the hand to the side of your face, placing the thumb near your ear.
Slide the tip of the thumb down along your jawbone until it reaches your chin.
Keep the palm facing inward toward your cheek while the thumb traces the jaw line.
Use a calm, neutral face while signing — the meaning is clear from the location alone.
tip: Born from the string of a bonnet tied under the chin — that is why female signs live near the jaw.

steps: Hold both hands in bent B shapes, with the fingers curved and the thumbs alongside.
Raise both hands to your shoulders, letting the fingertips touch down on them.
Tap your shoulders once or twice with the fingertips, using a firm, short contact.
Keep the palms angled down toward your shoulders as the fingertips make contact.
Hold a steady, serious expression — this sign names a duty, so sign it with weight.
tip: Think of the weight of a duty resting on your shoulders — tap twice for ‘responsibility,’ one long hold for ‘you are responsible.’

steps: Shape both hands into open-A hands, with the thumbs raised and slightly forward.
Hold the hands in front of your chest, with the thumbs pointing toward each other.
Move both hands in a small circular motion, keeping them near each other.
Keep the palms facing each other while the thumbs angle up and down.
Wear a friendly, engaged expression — this sign describes people interacting together.
tip: One sign covers associate, socialize, mingle, and hang out with — the ‘associated’ sense comes from context, not a separate sign.

steps: Hold both hands flat and open, with the fingers extended and together.
Raise both hands to the sides of your head, near your ears or temples.
Move both hands forward together in one short, even motion.
Keep the palms facing each other as the hands travel forward.
Direct your eyes and attention forward, showing concentration on the task.
tip: This is the sign Lifeprint glosses ATTENTION-[focus, concentrate, pay-attention] — it covers all three meanings.
